title: Improving the lower bound on the Laughlin gap: An SDP search
abstract: A recent preprint by OpenAI resolved the spherical fermionic Laughlin spectral-gap conjecture for the full $V_1$ interaction by a Fock-space inequality: $H_Q^2\ge γH_Q$ on the lowest-Landau-level Fock space for all large flux $Q$ and every $γ$ below $0.0461673\ldots$, so that the gap above the Laughlin state at filling $1/3$ is at least $1/25$. That proof, with its original constant, has also been formalized in Lean. We show that the same argument supports a much larger constant. Two sharper estimates, a product-twirl bound for the three-body tail and a staircase price for the four-body allowance, raise the constant above $0.0601$ without changing the original certificate. Treating the auxiliary operators as the variables of a semidefinite program (SDP) and enlarging the finite set of orbital modes on which they act then gives $H_Q^2\geγH_Q$ for every $γ<γ_*=0.2190037845063196\ldots$, certified by exact rational arithmetic. Consequently the gap above the Laughlin state is at least $1/5$ for all sufficiently large spheres, and the untruncated planar $V_1$ Hamiltonian has positive spectrum bounded below by $γ_*$, uniformly in particle number and angular momentum. A heuristic extrapolation of the SDP optima suggests that auxiliary operators of the present form can give at most about $0.222$, while exact diagonalization of finite systems places the true gap near $0.4$. A larger family of auxiliary operators could push the bound further towards the true gap, and the SDP formulation makes such families easy to test. The proof of the improvement and the SDP search were completed by the AI model Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic) under the author's direction.
summary: This paper significantly improves the theoretical lower bound on the spectral gap of the Laughlin state for interacting fermions using advanced mathematical optimization techniques. By formulating the problem as a Semidefinite Program (SDP) and systematically enlarging the mathematical constraints, the authors derive a much larger, rigorously certified gap constant. This advances the understanding of ground state properties in strongly correlated electron systems.
main_problem: The paper aims to improve the lower bound on the spectral gap of the Laughlin state for the full V1 interaction in a system of fermions on a sphere.
main_result: The authors establish a significantly larger lower bound for the gap, $\gamma^* \approx 0.219$, using Semidefinite Programming (SDP) techniques, implying the spectrum is bounded below by this value.
method: The core method involves formulating the gap problem as a semidefinite program (SDP) by treating auxiliary operators as variables and systematically enlarging the set of orbital modes considered.
model_or_system: The system is modeled by fermions interacting via the V1 pseudopotential Hamiltonian on a sphere, particularly analyzed at filling $1/3$. The analysis relies on operator inequalities of the form $H_Q^2 \ge \gamma H_Q$.
key_observables: The primary observable is the Laughlin spectral gap, quantified by the constant $\gamma$ in the inequality $H_Q^2 \ge \gamma H_Q$.
important_parameters: The analysis is concerned with the thermodynamic limit (large flux $Q$) and the specific filling fraction of $1/3$.
main_assumptions: The improvement relies on the assumption that the SDP formulation can capture the true gap, although exact diagonalization suggests the true gap might be higher ($\approx 0.4$).
figures_summary: The notes mention Table 1 summarizing various rigorous constants $\gamma$ achieved through different bounding techniques, culminating in the final SDP-derived value $\gamma^*$.
paper_structure: The paper builds upon previous work by first establishing the inequality structure, then introducing sharper bounds (product-twirl, staircase price), and finally employing the SDP search over enlarged orbital modes to derive the improved, rigorously certified constant $\gamma^*$.
why_interesting: The rigorous mathematical techniques (SDP, rational arithmetic verification) applied to a fundamental problem in fractional quantum Hall physics provide a powerful template for bounding spectral gaps in strongly correlated electron models.
